title: 1.5.16 Keep Two, Drop Two
description: Describe a bus route to a stranger. Two details stay, two go, and you have to justify all four. AI-graded with hints.

aiGrader.rubricTitle: Keep Two, Drop Two — AI-graded rubric
aiGrader.prompt:
You are describing a bus route to someone who has never been to your town.

1. Name two details you would KEEP, and say why each one matters.

2. Name two details you would LEAVE OUT, and say why each one does not matter.

3. State the test you used to decide. One sentence.

4. Now change the problem: the person is colour-blind and cannot read the route number from a distance. Does that change which details you keep? Say what moves, and why.

rubric.title: Two kept details, each with a reason
rubric.description: Student names two specific details they would keep - typically the stop to get on at and the stop to get off at - and says why each matters. Credit any pair whose absence would genuinely leave the listener unable to complete the journey. Deny if fewer than two, or if reasons are missing.

rubric.title: Two dropped details, each with a reason
rubric.description: Student names two specific details they would leave out - the colour of the bus, the name of each street, the driver, the upholstery - and says why each does not matter. The reason must be about the listener's actions, not about the detail being boring or obvious. Deny if fewer than two, or if a dropped detail is actually load-bearing.

rubric.title: Q3: states the abstraction test
rubric.description: Student articulates the test: does dropping this detail change what the person has to do? Wording will vary - 'would they still be able to get there', 'does it change their actions'. Deny if the stated test is about whether a detail is interesting, true, or short.

rubric.title: Q4: recognises that abstraction is relative to the problem
rubric.description: Student sees that changing the person changes which details are load-bearing - a detail previously dropped (such as the bus colour, or the route number's appearance) may now need keeping, or a new detail is needed. Credit any answer showing the kept/dropped line moved because the problem moved. Deny if the student says nothing changes, or repeats their first answer unchanged.
